description: We're SAAI, a Trivandrum team tackling "Abandoned but Not Forgotten," telling the stories of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. We love space exploration, planets & moons, astrophysics, satellites and hardware. We're looking for teammates skilled in storytelling, writing, graphic design, video/animation or web development to turn mission history into an engaging experience. Beginners welcome! We speak English and Hindi.
summary: An interactive map that lets people explore NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars through first-person stories, before-and-after timelines, and the engineering lessons each machine left behind.
details:
Graveyard of Firsts is an interactive web map that tells the stories of NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. Users choose a world, tap a landing site, and read a first-person story from machines such as Apollo 11’s Eagle, Surveyor 3, Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity. Each site has a “Then” view (the mission) and a “Now” view (what remains today), plus a “What it taught us” lesson about engineering and exploration.

Our goal is to make mission history personal and easy to explore, so students and the public see these machines as more than debris. It is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages, and works on phones and laptops in light or dark mode, with keyboard-accessible controls. Content is based on NASA mission histories and landing records. We chose first-person storytelling because it turns data into something memorable. We also prioritized factual accuracy, accessibility and a design that doesn’t use NASA logos or branding.
